[00:00] Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll do a quick round and then surface the usage numbers and some cost scenarios, uh Lena will take notes, um kia — (laugh) sorry Lena — Lena will take notes.

[00:27] Devon: hi, Devon, platform, quick note — we had one networking flake last thursday when we tried the private endpoint so want to make sure that doesn't block.

[00:45] Samira: ok quick go over numbers — blueharbor reported ~2.2k calls/day average, 1.8m tokens/day, 99.6% success. error spikes correlate with larger (>3k token) requests and a small KV cache miss pattern — i think the transcriber said KV cash in my notes, ha.
[01:10] Priya: that aligns with finance, monthly spend is roughly $42k current (hosted) but with anticipated growth to 120k if feature flags flip on in q4. we want to understand a dedicated commitment that flattens unit cost.
[01:28] Samira: totally. high level: hosted is easiest short term; dedicated cuts per-token by about 38% at the volume you shared, plus better burst predictability. tradeoff is commit/commit length.
[01:41] Alex: can you explain burst capacity? how do we avoid throttles during peak checkout traffic?
[01:48] Ethan: we recommend a baseline dedicated pool sized for 95th-percentile throughput, with burst capacity that can auto-scale into spare cluster capacity or fall back to hosted routing. fallbacks add a 100-200ms tail penalty in some routes.
[02:05] Jordan: is that an SLO we can promise? our product team needs a 200ms 95p for search completions.
[02:12] Ethan: depends on model and sequence length — on our measured sample for your small models we saw 95p at ~180ms on dedicated, hosted fallback went to ~320ms in worst case for long seqs. i'll share the raw benchmark.
[02:30] Maya: and quality — if we quantize for cost, do we risk user-facing regressions?
[02:35] Ethan: there's some model-dependent degradation, quantization profiles we recommend usually keep human-visible quality unchanged for short prompts; longer context generation can show artifacts. we can stage a canary with your eval set.
[02:51] Priya: finance question — what's the contract cadence? monthly or annual? we prefer quarterly if possible.
[02:58] Samira: we can do monthly reserved capacity with a month-to-month pilot, or a discounted annual commit. the pilot pricing spreadsheet (I'll send) shows the breakpoint where dedicated is cheaper than hosted.
[03:12] Devon: security blockers: we need SAML SSO config, audit logs to our SIEM, and KMS integration. also a note about egress — we need to ensure no outbound traffic to unknown endpoints.
[03:26] Lena: noted, security docs link: https://redwood.example.com/security/blueharbor (placeholder)
[03:31] Maya: we tried the private deploy trial — one issue was the onprem package couldn't mount our HSM emulator, error code 0x9a7. might be infra on our end but we flagged it.
[03:44] Ethan: ok we'll pair on that, could be a volume mount permission.
[03:48] (overlap) Priya: quick clarifying Q — does dedicated still send logs to our tenant SIEM or do we need a separate forwarder?
[03:55] Samira: logs are forwarded; for private we can do direct push via your syslog endpoint or S3 with lifecycle. we'll detail options in the security pack.
[04:08] Alex: timeline — if we accept dedicated pilot, what's onboarding ETA?
[04:12] Samira: typical dedicated-onboard for accounts this size is 3–4 weeks: week 1 config, week 2 staging and benchmarks, week 3 pilot run, week 4 ramp. can compress to 2–3 weeks with prioritized infra access.
[04:27] Maya: okay good.

[04:44] Priya: could you include cost per 1M tokens for each profile? that helps our forecast model.
[04:49] Samira: yes will include hosted/dedicated/quantized scenarios.
[04:52] Jordan: small thing — can we set a guardrail to prevent model rollouts that spike latency? we'd like automatic rejection if 95p increases >20%.
[05:00] Ethan: we have rollback policies built into the rollout engine; we can wire in your metric threshold and halt rollouts automatically.
[05:08] Maya: competitors — a few infra folks asked about Anthropic because of claimed latency but the team's worried about vendor lock; Vertex AI was mentioned for native GCP integration.
[05:22] Samira: noted. from a risk lens we emphasize multi-variant routing and transparent cost breakdowns.
[05:30] Devon: question on billing: can we get token-level breakouts by route? e.g., search vs recommendations vs triage?
[05:38] Lena: yes we already send per-route usage exports; i'll include the last 30 day CSV in the follow-up.
